provenanceNote: Skatteverket's own organization number, published by Skatteverket about itself. Third digit is 2, so by 4 § lagen (1974:174) it cannot be any person's personnummer -- a personnummer's third digit is the first digit of its month and so is 0 or 1. Covered by the organization-number carve-out in CLAUDE.md: no living bearer, and Swedish company registration data is public by law. Carries no referenceDate because an organization number encodes no birth date, so no century has to be inferred.
The same Skatteverket number without its separator, asserting that the canonical form does not depend on how the caller wrote it. Third digit 2; see the entry above for the carve-out.

Input already in twelve-digit PeOrgNr form, so the canonical form is unchanged rather than gaining a second prefix. Third digit of the ten-digit body is 6, so 4 § lagen (1974:174) places it outside the personnummer space. Used as the canonical-form example in README.md and the design spec since Plan 1.

Bolagsverket's own organization number, published by Bolagsverket about itself. Third digit is 2, so by 4 § lagen (1974:174) it cannot be any person's personnummer. Asserts the nullable accessors are actually null: an organization number encodes neither a birth date nor a gender, which is the case the SchemeResult refactor was built for.

Statistiska centralbyrån's own organization number, published by SCB about itself. Third digit is 2, so by 4 § lagen (1974:174) it cannot be any person's personnummer. Pins all four renderings. Display drops the 16 legal-person marker to give 202100-3062, the form Swedish organization numbers are actually written in, and Short is identical because there is no century to elide and no bearer whose age a +/- separator could report. Note Short therefore needs no referenceDate, where a Swedish personal number's would fail with ReferenceDateRequired. Masked keeps the prefix and blanks the last four, uniformly with every other scheme.

A published Skatteverket personal number in ten-digit short form. It is NOT rejected outright -- the personal-number scheme claims it, which is the correct answer -- but the organization scheme refuses it on the third-digit rule, and that refusal is what this fixture exists to pin. Its third digit is 0 because that digit is the first digit of the month, which is exactly why 4 § lagen (1974:174) fixes an organization number's at 2 or above. There is no separate 'third digit below 2' case to write: a personnummer is such a number.

Skatteverket's organization number with its check digit incremented, so the value fails Luhn and no bearer can exist. Also pins the failure-precedence rule: the personal-number scheme answers impossible-date for this input, because read as a personnummer its month is 21, and checksum-mismatch is the more specific answer since the third digit already established which kind of number it is.

Skatteverket's own organization number, third digit 2, under options that exclude organization numbers. The failure must be scheme-not-allowed rather than not-an-identity-number: the caller's own option is the reason, and reporting 'unrecognised' would hide that. This is why the scheme runs even when the option is false -- a scheme the dispatcher skipped could not report why it refused.

The sole-proprietorship case, and the most misunderstood behaviour in the package. A Swedish sole proprietorship has no separate organization number: its organization number IS the owner's personal number, identical digits. SCB states this directly -- 'För fysiska personer, enskilda näringsidkare, motsvaras PeOrgNr av personnumret'. So such a value resolves as se-personal-number with isPerson() true, and that is correct rather than a defect. No parser setting recovers the distinction; it is contextual, not structural. Marked skatteverket rather than public-organization on purpose: this is exactly the case the organization-number carve-out excludes, because the number has a third digit of 0 or 1 and therefore is a person's number. Consumers matching people must treat isPerson() as load-bearing.
